Bits of metal snapped and jumped away from the edge, the band positively shrieking against the assault. The blade cracked the seam open with a final twist, the band fracturing in half. Sparks exploded across the hallway. Gabriel threw the knife aside and ripped at the cuff, pulling the sharp internal teeth free from ruined flesh — no wonder it wouldn’t rotate — and flinching as some kind of off colored fluid sprayed randomly from the damaged mechanism to mix with the blood that was spreading across the floor. Gabriel threw it away from himself and down the corridor without thinking. The voltage that arced through the metal as it left his hand reached back like a last insult and ran up his arm and into his teeth, sending him flinching into himself with a sharp snap that numbed his entire spine and smeared the lights behind his eyes. The hallway took a deep breath when the screaming stopped, and for a moment, no one moved. Nea’s arms were shaking. She pushed herself backward, staring at Wesker’s still form as if expecting him to leap up and resume rearranging their limbs any second. “Is he... Did we just...” Dwight rolled off the pinned shoulder and got to his feet on the second try, scooping Nea up by the elbow. “Come on. We gotta go.” She allowed herself to be hauled swiftly away, reluctantly glancing back one more time at the violence that was spread out across the hall before vanishing around the corner. Jake didn’t move at first, chest rising too fast, eyes flicking between Wesker and the wrecked band on the floor. Then he swore under his breath, grabbed Gabriel by the back of his shirt, and pulled him out of the potential swing radius. After all that, he wasn’t about to risk the killer regaining his senses and decided to take revenge. “You with me?” Jake’s voice pitched low, urgency bleeding through as he tapped Gabriel’s face lightly, trying to get his eyes to focus. “Good. I’m good. Just — numb.” Gabriel coughed. “Go. Go — I’m right behind you.” Jake squeezed his collar once and let go. “Catch up or I’m coming back for you.” “Go. Make sure they get out. I’m alright. Just need a minute.” Jake gave a short nod and jogged off after the others. The corridor was suddenly very large and very empty. The piece of metal lying 20 feet away from Wesker’s hand was still leaking tiny, spitting complaints into the air. The man himself hadn’t moved since the cuff came free. He was bleeding against the cement, the harsh smell of iron and something sour filled the space, and Gabriel couldn’t tell in the moment if he had even survived. Blinking away the shock haze, he rolled to his knees and hauled himself closer. He wasn’t sure why he was keeping his voice down — habit, maybe. Something in him didn’t want to wake anything else. He touched two fingers to Wesker’s neck and waited past the first nothing. The skin was hot and damp and smelled wrong. For a few tense moments, he couldn’t find a pulse. What even happened to killers if they died? Did they have a place they were rebuilt to the way the survivors did? Gabriel frowned and shifted his hand slightly, and there it was: a small, stubborn movement against his fingertips, a flutter that wasn’t rhythm but could be again if given time. He let out a breath he hadn’t noticed holding. He turned Wesker’s wrist gently with his free hand and watched, fascinated and horrified, as the torn edges of skin twitched and tried to think about knitting. It wasn’t a miracle. It wasn’t fast. It was work performed by something that had been denied work for weeks. Thin strands of damaged pulp reached out for others, slowly trying to staunch bleeding and rebuild muscle. On reflex, or possibly some buried compassion, Gabriel pulled an old bandana out of his back pocket and wound it tightly around the gore. At least he wasn’t going to bleed out on the floor after everything. The rest... well that was out of Gabriel’s hands now. Time would tell if it was all worth it, or if they had just repaired their own execution. He got up slowly on unsteady legs, hissing lightly as waking nerves protested the movement. The broken cuff still sparked gently against the floor, whatever fluid it had been spraying now collecting in a puddle around the shards. He put his heel on it and drove his weight down until the housing buckled and the last of the teeth bent in on themselves for good measure, scattering what remained with the side of his shoe. Gabriel leaned against the wall with one hand and worked his way to join up with the rest of the survivors. The Fog coiled around Wesker, waiting for them to leave so it could take what was left of him home. Chapter 15 – Recalibration The Fog didn’t release him — it dropped him. Discarded back to the station, barely short of tumbling down the front steps. Cold tile rushed up to meet him, the impact punching air out of abused lungs and pain into every inch of his body. His spine arched, air rasping in through clenched teeth. Every nerve screamed at once, awareness wrenched cruelly back from the void. Everything either burned or didn’t register at all. His body couldn’t decide which. The world existed in fragments: the buzz of failing lights, the taste of metal in his teeth, a flash of white restraint and hands digging into limbs he could barely control.
